newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 15.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning.

St George Bank Ltd said on Monday it would make an agreed A$2.65 billion takeover bid for fellow Sydney-based regional bank Advance Bank Australia Ltd. Analysts said the deal looked like it would proceed, the fifth time St George has attempted to merge or takeover another bank. Traders, however, will be watching the stocks for signs of predatory moves by the major local banks or international banks wanting an Australian foothold.

Executive chairman and founder Rupert Murdoch addresses shareholders at the annual meeting of the international media company in Adelaide this morning. News Corp's recent court win with Super League and the popularity of the film Independence Day has seen the share price recover strongly, aided by company executives forecasting a 20 percent rise in current year profits.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.84 (+0.49)
Company executives meet with New South Wales Premier Bob Carr and steel union executives to discuss the future of the Newcastle steelworks this morning.

The company's Ernest Henry base metals project in Queensland faces another potential stumbling block with a complaint by an aboriginal dance troupe that the project's power line would interfere with sacred sites.

The building products, sugar, and aluminium company said after the share market closed on Monday that first half earnings would most likely fall by 20 percent and the interim dividend would be cut by two cents. It said the only bright spot appeared to be its North American operations and the full year result could also be down by 20 percent if the first half trend continued.

The European Union said it is investigating the A$2.0 billion takeover of the transport group by Holland's Dutch PTT, examining the market dominance position of the merged group. TNT's second largest shareholder, Phillips and Drew Funds Management also said from London that a rival bid was possible and it would adopt a wait-and-see position regarding its 11.69 percent stake.
